Segment and filter copy-number windows

Source: R/read_counts.R
filter_windows.Rd

For each chromosome, split the windows at genome gaps, segment the values of mcols_id within each gap-free fragment with changepoint::cpt.mean(), and replace each window value by its segment median (seg_score). Windows are then removed if any of the following holds:

  • the window is more than twice as long as the shortest window of the chromosome (end - start used as length);

  • |seg_score - genome median| > std_th * genome SD (median and SD of the raw mcols_id values over all chromosomes);

  • |seg_score - chromosome median of retained seg_score| > std_th * genome SD;

  • seg_score == 0 or seg_score is NA.

Only windows with non-NA values <= 20 are segmented, and only fragments with more than 20 such windows; all other windows get NA and are removed. If cpt.mean() fails on a fragment, all its windows get the fragment median.

Usage

filter_windows(
  wins_grl,
  gaps,
  mcols_id,
  std_th = 2,
  cpt_arg = list(method = "PELT", penalty = "MBIC", test.stat = "Normal", minseglen = 5,
    class = TRUE)
)

Arguments

wins_grl

A GRangesList (one element per chromosome) containing the numeric metadata column mcols_id.

gaps

A GRanges of genome gap regions.

mcols_id

Character scalar. Metadata column to segment, e.g. "raw_cn".

std_th

Positive numeric scalar. SD multiplier for filtering. We use 0.5 (sometimes 0.35).

cpt_arg

List of arguments passed to changepoint::cpt.mean().

Value

A GRangesList with the same names as wins_grl holding only the retained windows; metadata columns are inherited, plus a numeric column named paste0(mcols_id, "_seg_score").

Examples

set.seed(1)
gr <- GenomicRanges::GRanges("chr1", IRanges::IRanges(seq(1, by = 1000, length.out = 60),
                                                      width = 1000))
gr$raw_cn <- c(rnorm(30, 2, 0.1), rnorm(30, 4, 0.1))
gaps <- GenomicRanges::GRanges("chr1", IRanges::IRanges(10001, 12000))
res <- filter_windows(GenomicRanges::GRangesList(chr1 = gr), gaps, "raw_cn",
                      std_th = 2)
length(res$chr1)
#> [1] 48
